title: Warming Up Cold-Start CTR Prediction by Learning Item-Specific Feature Interactions

problem.claim: Cold-start CTR prediction for newly introduced items is difficult because they initially lack interaction records.

gap.claim: Existing methods generally enhance item ID embeddings within global feature-interaction models, which can overshadow sparse-data new items with items having abundant interactions.

contributions.claim: EmerG learns item-specific feature interaction patterns for cold-start CTR prediction by using hypernetworks to generate item-specific feature graphs from item characteristics and processing them with a GNN.
EmerG uses a customized message-passing mechanism intended to capture feature interactions at any order.

EmerG applies meta learning across item CTR prediction tasks, optimizing hypernetwork and GNN parameters while adjusting only a minimal set of item-specific parameters within each task to reduce overfitting under limited data.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present EmerG as a novel approach that warms up cold-start CTR prediction by learning item-specific feature interaction patterns.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on benchmark datasets.
The authors report that EmerG consistently performs best when new items have no, few, or sufficient instances.

narrative_sequence.summary: New recommendation items begin without interaction records, making accurate CTR prediction important for revenue and user experience.
Global feature interaction approaches can favor items with abundant interactions over sparse-data new items.
EmerG generates item-specific feature graphs with hypernetworks and processes them using a specialized GNN.
Meta learning transfers hypernetwork and GNN parameters across item CTR tasks while limiting task-specific adaptation.
Benchmark experiments are reported for settings ranging from no instances to sufficient instances of new items.

source_observation.claim: The approach generates feature interactions conditioned on item characteristics instead of relying only on global interactions.

interpretation.claim: Conditioning interaction structure on entity characteristics may help models represent heterogeneous behavior under sparse observations.

application.claim: For other cold-start prediction tasks, consider adapting interaction structure to entity-specific information.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy generalizes beyond the reported CTR prediction setting.

unknowns: Detailed hypernetwork, graph, message-passing, and meta-learning formulations
Operational definition of no, few, and sufficient new-item instances
